Definition: a yard (as inclosed by a fence); also a hamlet (as similarly surrounded with walls)
BiblicalUsage: A court is an enclosed yard, and the word stretches from the tabernacle to the king's house. The court of the tabernacle is hung with fine linen, Solomon builds the inner court of the temple with hewn stone and cedar, the people make booths in the courts of the house of God, and Esther stands in the inner court of the king.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the court is where the people meet God and where the queen risks her life to meet the king. Both courts are enclosed, and both are entered only on the terms of the one who owns them.
RelatedPeople: Moses; King Solomon; Queen Esther; Nehemiah
RelatedEvents: The Tabernacle Is Built; Building of Solomon's Temple; Ezra Reads the Law; Esther Saves Her People
